title: Straight road, one lane over (~3.3 m)
shown: real adjacent-lane frame | raw splat | released Difix | our Difix reimplementation (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
caption: The splat was fitted on lane 0 only and is rendered where lane 1 actually drove. Released Difix sharpens but does not restore the missing lane paint; our driving-trained Difix restores most lane lines; the small U-Net blurs. Cars differ between passes (the lanes were driven at different times).
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: Lane change: sliding the camera 0 -> 3 -> 6 m off the recorded lane
shown: nearest real frame (only on the two real lanes) | raw | released Difix | our Difix (ref) | our U-Net | road prior | progressive splat
caption: The camera slides from the recorded lane to the next lane (3.3 m) and the one after (6.2 m). Real frames exist only where Para-Lane actually drove (shown as the nearest real frame of that lane, driven at another time, so traffic differs); in between there is no ground truth.
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: Two lanes over (~7.7 m), the widest Para-Lane test offset
shown: real far-lane frame | raw splat | released Difix | our Difix reimplementation (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
caption: At 7.7 m the splat has never seen most of the road surface. Every fixer produces a cleaner-looking image, but none recovers the real lane geometry reliably; lane agreement stays low (RESULTS section 5).
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: Curved road, two lanes over (about 5 m)
shown: real far-lane frame | raw splat | released Difix | our Difix reimplementation (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
caption: A held-out test road that bends 30-50 deg over about 110 m. Lane 0's splat is rendered where lane 2 actually drove. Our driving-trained Difix draws crisp lane lines, but not always where the real ones are: plausible is not the same as faithful. (The on-screen offset label differs slightly from the 5.3 m median offset of this clip.)
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: Under an elevated highway, dense traffic (about 4 m over)
scenario: lateral offset, hard shadows and traffic
shown: real adjacent-lane frame | raw splat | released Difix | our Difix reimplementation (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
caption: The hardest of the five test roads: hard shadows, pillars and the most traffic. Every method stays low here (best lane agreement 0.39 one lane over). Cars in the renders are whatever the splat and fixer produce; the lanes were driven at different times, so traffic differs from the real frame.
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: Camera height sweep: -1 m to +1 m
shown: (no real frame) | recorded real frame at 0 m | raw | released Difix | our Difix (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
caption: Lower or higher cameras (a sports car, a truck) see the road at a different angle. There is no real frame at another height, so this is a visual check only; the report scores the road region against a road-plane warp (RESULTS section 12) and against real car/scooter pairs on MV2.
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: Heading sweep: turning the camera +-15 deg
shown: real frame rotated by the exact homography (black = never seen by the real camera) | raw | released Difix | our Difix (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
caption: For a pure rotation the real frame can be warped exactly; black regions are parts of the scene the recorded camera never saw. Inside the seen region every method stays close to the real frame (heading is not what breaks the splat); the newly revealed regions at the image border are where splats and fixers improvise.
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: Progressive 3D update: before / after (no fixer at render time)
shown: real | original splat | refined without fixer (control) | progressive with Difix-FT | progressive with our Difix
caption: The splat itself is refined with fixed pseudo-views at +-3 m and +-6 m (Difix3D+ progressive update), then rendered WITHOUT any fixer. On scene_16 the lane lines come back in 3D (lane F1 0.18 -> 0.90 at ~3 m); on scene_17 the same procedure helps far less, so this gain is scene-dependent.
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: Road-surface prior: before / after (no generative model)
shown: real | raw splat | splat fitted with the LiDAR road-surface prior
caption: A height/slope field fitted to LiDAR pulls road Gaussians onto the road plane and flattens them. No generative model is involved, so nothing can be invented; lane lines are sharper off-path.
attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

title: EUVS / MARS: a different route through the same place (transfer)
shown: real test frame | raw splat | released Difix-ref | NVIDIA Fixer | our Difix (ref) | our U-Net
caption: The test traversal takes another route through the same place (median 5.5 m and 89 deg from the nearest training camera). Only the released, generically trained fixers help here; our Para-Lane-trained models do not transfer (RESULTS section 13).
attribution: Data: EUVS benchmark (ICCV 2025) MARS scenes (MARS, CVPR 2024; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). CS 566, non-commercial.

title: HUGSIM (nuScenes): shifting the ego car 0 -> 3 m
scenario: lateral offset in a released simulator scene
shown: (no real frame) | raw HUGSIM render | released Difix | NVIDIA Fixer | Difix-FT | our U-Net
caption: HUGSIM's released reconstruction rendered 0-3 m off the logged path. Detector agreement with the 0 m render falls ~16% by 3 m; NVIDIA Fixer recovers most, our Para-Lane-trained models do not transfer (our U-Net washes out vehicles; RESULTS section 8).
attribution: Data: HUGSIM released nuScenes scenes (MIT); nuScenes by Motional, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. CS 566, non-commercial.

title: HUGSIM closed loop with the LTF policy (no fixer)
shown: policy's three front camera views + bird's-eye view (ego, other vehicles, planned path)
caption: One closed-loop rollout (hard scenario, seed 0): HD-Score 0.78, route completion 1.00. Played at 5 fps (sim runs at 4 Hz). Across 25 scenarios x 3 seeds the no-fixer HD-Score is 0.41 (RESULTS section 8).
attribution: Data: HUGSIM released nuScenes scenes (MIT); nuScenes by Motional, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. CS 566, non-commercial.
